headline: Banks working with Broadcom have reportedly started gathering $60 billion of financing to pay for AI chips for Anthropic and other companies.
score_reason: Lowered from 8 to 7: Bloomberg only says the money is starting to be gathered, from unnamed sources, and the deal has not been announced.
importance_line: Bloomberg says it is being watched as a test of whether investors still want to fund the AI buildout despite public backlash against data centers, which matters to AI chip buyers such as Anthropic and to Broadcom, but it rests on unnamed sources and nothing has been announced.
summary: Bloomberg reports, citing people with knowledge of the matter, that banks working with Broadcom have started gathering $60 billion of financing to pay for AI chips for Anthropic and other companies: a $42 billion slice that is repaid first and an $18 billion riskier slice led by Blackstone, which is committing $9 billion from its funds. This follows a 1 Oct 2026 Reuters report that Broadcom would lend Anthropic up to $42 billion to lease its chips, but the Bloomberg report does not say how the two are related; the deal has not been announced and a Broadcom representative declined to comment.
notes: Original outlet Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/broadcom-starts-amassing-60-billion-to-fund-chips-for-anthropic) was blocked (HTTP 403); wrote from the same Bloomberg wire text on Yahoo Finance, so source and url are Yahoo Finance's. Based on unnamed sources. The article does not say how the $42 billion tranche relates to the $42 billion Broadcom lease lending to Anthropic reported 1 Oct 2026, so the entry does not link the two.
